definition: A system composed of multiple AI agents that interact, communicate, or collaborate (and sometimes compete) to accomplish tasks.
details: Multi-agent LLM systems can divide labor across specialized sub-agents (e.g., a planner, a coder, a reviewer), potentially improving robustness and task decomposition compared to a single monolithic agent.
story: Picture hiring a brilliant new assistant on their first morning — smart, motivated, but with no idea how anything in your office actually works. It plans a little, acts a little, looks at the result, and then decides what to do next. It is the difference between a search engine and a helper who actually finishes the task. The model stops being a one-shot answer machine and becomes a coworker that checks its own work. That loop of reason, act, and observe is Multi-Agent System.
